Source. `localIjToCell()` first consumes the attacker-controlled local-IJ pair by starting the `ij -> ijk` conversion. On the exact witness this call is reached with `origin = 0x200f202020202020`, `ij->i = -14671840`, and `ij->j = -2147483648`.
`ijToIjk()` materializes the caller's local-IJ pair as raw cube coordinates `ijk = {-14671840, -2147483648, 0}` before normalization.
Because `c->i` is negative, the first normalization block runs and transforms the raw triple to `c = {0, -2132811808, 14671840}`. That intermediate state feeds the next `c->j < 0` block.

With the step-3 state, `c->j` is still negative. `c->i -= c->j` stays in range, but `c->k -= c->j` computes `14671840 - (-2132811808) = 2147483648`, overflowing 32-bit signed `int` at line 226. The saved build uses `-O1 -fsanitize=address` without `-fwrapv` or UBSan, so the exact `ijk` contents after this step are not source-defined by the staged artifacts.

After `ijToIjk()` returns, `localIjToCell()` forwards the unchanged attacker-controlled `origin` word together with the post-normalization `ijk` object into `localIjkToCell()`. This is the source-level handoff that carries `origin` into the later base-cell decode.

int res = H3_GET_RESOLUTION(origin);
int originBaseCell = H3_GET_BASE_CELL(origin);
anchors.note: `localIjkToCell()` decodes the attacker-controlled raw `origin` word. For witness `0x200f202020202020`, these macros produce `res == 0` and `originBaseCell == 121`, fixing the row later used in `baseCellNeighbors`.
Because `res == 0`, execution takes the special base-cell conversion branch instead of the general digit-building logic used for higher resolutions.

Root cause. This guard only rejects components greater than 1; it does not validate the `Direction` returned by `_unitIjkToDigit()` before that value is used as a neighbor-table index. For this witness, the earlier `_ijkNormalize()` arithmetic has already overflowed `int`, so the exact `ijk` triple here is not source-defined from the staged artifacts alone. What the saved crash does establish is that execution reaches line 326, so this check did not return `E_FAILED`.

In the resolution-0 branch, `_unitIjkToDigit()` is the only source of `dir`. Since step 6 fixed `originBaseCell = 121` and the later fault lands exactly one element past the final `baseCellNeighbors[122][7]` row, the observed execution must have produced `dir == 7` here. The staged artifacts do not record the exact post-overflow `ijk` components that led to that result.
`localIjkToCell()` uses the decoded base cell and the unchecked direction value in `_getBaseCellNeighbor(originBaseCell, dir)`. On the observed execution that means `_getBaseCellNeighbor(121, 7)`.

Sink. `_getBaseCellNeighbor()` indexes the global table as `baseCellNeighbors[121][7]`. The second dimension is size 7 with valid columns `0..6`, and base cell 121 is the final row of the `122 x 7` array declared at line 38, so this 4-byte read lands exactly one element past global `baseCellNeighbors`. The saved ASan trace reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at this line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of `baseCellNeighbors`.
